topic: Target-span completeness for rank-deficient proxy transport in a strictly positive finite latent-shift SCM, with weak-rank Anderson–Rubin projection inference and the Expedia hotel-ranking application.

open_problems.open_problem: In the strictly positive finite latent-shift SCM with an unknown full-column-rank proxy channel, is Q(Y|do(x)) identified exactly when Q(W) belongs to col(P(W|E,x)), even when P(W|E,x) is rank-deficient?

source_refs.claim: Theorem 1 gives the target causal functional under full source rank; Appendix B.2 instead weakens the proxy channel and does not analyze target-specific identification under deficient source rank.
source_refs.author: Manuel Iglesias-Alonso, Felix Schur, Julius von Kügelgen, Jonas Peters

source_refs.claim: Proposition 2.3 identifies a linear functional of a nonunique bridge iff its loading annihilates the operator null space, but it does not prove a full-observed-law SCM converse for proxy transport.
source_refs.author: Jeffrey Zhang, Wei Li, Wang Miao, Eric Tchetgen Tchetgen

source_refs.claim: Theorem 3 identifies a target predictor when a full-rank set of source environments spans proxy-induced latent-equivalence-class operators, not a target-specific interventional iff under deficient source rank.
source_refs.author: Zahra Rahiminasab, Reza Soumi, Arto Klami, Samuel Kaski

source_refs.excerpt: The exact nullspace orthocomplement criterion is already published

open_problems.why_unsolved: Iglesias-Alonso et al. prove a stronger full-source-rank sufficient condition and show generic failure by making the proxy channel itself rank-deficient. Zhang et al. already subsume the abstract solution-independence algebra, a collision also recorded by the failed prior proposal, while Rahiminasab et al. give a full-cross-domain-rank prediction analogue. None establishes the narrower causal frontier with injective M, deficient source variation, and a particular target Q(W), or realizes failure by two strictly positive SCMs that agree on every supplied P(E,W,X,Y) cell and Q(W). Thus novelty can only rest on the target-specific full-SCM iff and its realizable converse, not on nullspace annihilation alone.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A necessary-and-sufficient SCM identification theorem stating Q(Y|do(x))=P(Y|E,x)lambda for every solution of P(W|E,x)lambda=Q(W), with solution independence and paired strictly positive full-law countermodels whenever Q(W) lies outside the column space.

writing_exemplar.why: It is the closest causal-target and data-pattern paper, including the source/target proxy setup and Expedia ranking application.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Latent population shifts change causal effects -> target outcomes are unavailable but a proxy law is observed -> full source diversity yields a balancing functional -> determine the exact target-specific frontier under rank-deficient source diversity

method_exemplars.technique: Use the affine solution-set/null-space argument of Proposition 2.3 to prove that all balancing solutions induce the same linear functional, then add an SCM-realizability converse.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The desired solution-independence statement is its finite-dimensional analogue, while the new work begins exactly where the abstract bridge argument stops: preserving the complete supplied law with positive SCMs.

method_exemplars.technique: Adapt the reduced observed-law parametrization and joint multinomial limit calculation after replacing the fixed full-rank pseudoinverse by a target-specific balancing relation.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It estimates the same transported interventional distribution from the same source joint law and target proxy law, albeit only at fixed full source rank.

open_problems.open_problem: Construct a uniformly valid Anderson–Rubin projection confidence set for theta_x=P(Y|E,x)lambda under B_x lambda=Q(W) when rank(B_x) changes, balancing weights diverge, and multinomial moment covariance is singular.

source_refs.claim: Its Wald interval uses a pointwise delta-method CLT under full rank, and its experiments show error increasing with the condition number of P(W|E,x).
source_refs.author: Manuel Iglesias-Alonso, Felix Schur, Julius von Kügelgen, Jonas Peters

source_refs.claim: The paper projects Anderson–Rubin confidence regions onto subvectors and characterizes boundedness in linear structural IV models.
source_refs.author: Jean-Marie Dufour, Mohamed Taamouti

source_refs.claim: SR-AR tests have uniform asymptotic size without identification-strength or covariance-eigenvalue bounds, but the paper's subvector theory assumes the nuisance parameter is strongly identified.
source_refs.author: Donald W. K. Andrews, Patrik Guggenberger

source_refs.excerpt: the phase diagram and projection confidence set are conjectures
Rewrite Conjecture 2 with a fully specified theta estimator, variance estimator, joint Gaussian limit

open_problems.why_unsolved: AR inversion avoids dividing by a weak first stage, and Andrews–Guggenberger handle singular covariance for full-vector moment tests. Here theta_x is a projection of the joint restrictions B_x lambda=Q(W) and P(Y|E,x)lambda=theta_x, with lambda a nuisance that may be nonunique or unbounded. Dufour–Taamouti is linear-IV-specific, Andrews–Guggenberger's subvector result assumes strongly identified nuisance parameters, and the prior CausalSmith attempts never specified a complete theta statistic, variance estimator, joint limit, and coverage event. Shared multinomial cells and simplex identities add structural covariance degeneracy, so neither a fixed chi-square rule nor pointwise Gaussian calibration is justified uniformly.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A computable inverted-test confidence set for theta_x, allowed to be empty, disconnected, or nonshrinking, with a theorem proving uniform asymptotic coverage over strong, weak, changing-rank, and singular-covariance triangular arrays without compact or strongly identified lambda.

writing_exemplar.why: It supplies the empirical target, observed moments, conditioning failure mode, and Expedia consumer that robust inference must repair.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Proxy transport yields a plug-in causal estimator -> near rank failure invalidates Wald calibration -> Expedia-like domain diversity may be weak -> invert rank-robust moments and project onto the causal effect

method_exemplars.technique: Invert a full-parameter AR region and project it by optimization onto the scalar target.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The requested set is exactly a projection problem with weakly identified balancing coefficients as nuisance parameters.

method_exemplars.technique: Adapt singularity-robust standardization that retains stochastic moment directions and adds a rejection condition for nonstochastic directions, with uniform drifting-sequence size control.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Multinomial proxy-transport moments have the exact covariance singularities that ordinary studentization cannot handle, but the proof must be extended to an unbounded profiled nuisance.

method_exemplars.technique: Profile nuisance parameters from a GMM criterion and prove uniform subvector coverage across identification regimes.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It supplies the relevant uniform projection architecture; target transport changes the regular nuisance geometry to a changing-rank balancing fiber.

open_problems.open_problem: Determine the sharp minimax inference phase as Q(W) approaches col(B_x) and the nonzero singular values of B_x weaken, using a target-relevant balancing certificate rather than a global completeness eigenvalue.

source_refs.claim: The paper gives a strong-functional condition and debiased root-n inference when an inverse-problem nuisance is weakly identified or nonunique.
source_refs.author: Andrew Bennett, Nathan Kallus, Xiaojie Mao, Whitney Newey, Vasilis Syrgkanis, Masatoshi Uehara

source_refs.claim: Lemma 2.4 separates identification by null-space orthogonality from root-n estimability by membership in the actual adjoint range.
source_refs.author: Jeffrey Zhang, Wei Li, Wang Miao, Eric Tchetgen Tchetgen

source_refs.claim: Its asymptotic normality is pointwise at full rank, while simulation error grows rapidly as P(W|E,x) becomes ill-conditioned.
source_refs.author: Manuel Iglesias-Alonso, Felix Schur, Julius von Kügelgen, Jonas Peters

source_refs.excerpt: rho_n(P_n) is the sharp proximal identification-strength variable
rho_n depends on the minimum singular value of an unobserved operator

open_problems.why_unsolved: The banked completeness run left a three-region phase diagram conjectural and operationally unusable because its strength scalar depended on an unobserved operator. In target-span transport, neither sigma_min(B_x) nor distance from Q(W) to col(B_x) alone controls the causal functional: stability also depends on the target direction, the minimum-norm balancing representation, outcome loading, and multinomial covariance. Bennett et al. and Zhang et al. give the abstract strong-functional/range distinction but not this correlated two-sample probability experiment. Matching lower bounds must additionally follow factorization-preserving local SCM paths, not arbitrary perturbations of B_x.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A local asymptotic and minimax theorem giving an observable certificate that separates root-n Gaussian, slower-rate or nonregular, weak nonshrinking, and span-failure regimes, with an attaining estimator, efficiency bound where finite, and factorization-preserving lower bounds.

writing_exemplar.why: Its framing cleanly distinguishes recovery of a weak inverse nuisance from regular estimation of a target-relevant functional.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Balancing weights solve an unstable inverse problem -> the transported causal target can remain unique -> regularity needs a stronger target representer condition -> locate the exact rate and inference boundary for proxy transport

method_exemplars.technique: Port penalized minimax estimation of the primary and debiasing inverse solutions and the orthogonal asymptotic-linear expansion.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The transported effect is a linear functional of balancing solutions, precisely the weak-nuisance/strong-functional structure treated there.

method_exemplars.technique: Adapt tangent-space and adjoint-range calculations for efficiency of linear functionals when the inverse nuisance is unidentified or ill-posed.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It supplies the efficiency calculation needed to distinguish finite information from divergence as minimum-norm balancing weights explode.

method_exemplars.technique: Embed identification strength in drifting triangular arrays and derive regime-specific limits from one common expansion.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The transport phase must cover B_x sequences moving from stable balancing through weak rank to span failure without a preliminary rank decision.

open_problems.open_problem: When Q(W) is outside col(B_x), what is the sharp identified set for Q(Y|do(x)) over strictly positive finite latent-shift SCMs with an unknown full-column-rank P(W|U) that reproduce the entire source joint law and target proxy law?

source_refs.claim: Appendix B.2 gives one nonidentification construction but neither retains an injective proxy channel nor characterizes sharp effect bounds under deficient source rank.
source_refs.author: Manuel Iglesias-Alonso, Felix Schur, Julius von Kügelgen, Jonas Peters

source_refs.claim: The paper derives proxy-informed partial-identification bounds without completeness and bootstrap inference for smoothed endpoints, in a different proximal confounding model.
source_refs.author: AmirEmad Ghassami, Ilya Shpitser, Eric Tchetgen Tchetgen

source_refs.claim: AutoBounds reduces finite discrete SCM compatibility and sharp causal bounds to polynomial programming, but does not instantiate this shared-channel latent-shift transport model.
source_refs.author: Guilherme Duarte, Noam Finkelstein, Dean Knox, Jonathan Mummolo, Ilya Shpitser
source_refs.venue: Journal of the American Statistical Association

source_refs.excerpt: same bridge-operator nullspace and the same null-annihilator quotient certificate, but different sharp ATE sets
specify all observable cells, latent tables, bridge values, ATE loadings, and a Farkas multiplier

open_problems.why_unsolved: Failure of the target-span condition proves only that the identified set is not a singleton. The closest proxy-bound papers study single-domain proximal models or partly known measurement channels, while general polynomial machinery has not encoded this combination of a shared unknown injective proxy channel, source mixtures, invariant outcome mechanisms, strict positivity, every P(E,W,X,Y) cell, and Q(W). The rejected prior angle also found that an algebraic proxy nullspace can strictly exceed the perturbations realizable by nonnegative latent causal laws; it failed to verify a full positive endpoint construction and dual obstruction. The first unresolved step is therefore the exact SCM-realizable feasible set, not unconstrained nullspace optimization.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A finite polynomial, polyhedral, or analytic-dual characterization of the compatible transported-effect interval, with computable endpoints, strictly positive endpoint-attaining SCMs or dual sharpness certificates, collapse to the span functional on the identified face, and valid endpoint inference.

writing_exemplar.why: Its motivation moves directly from unverifiable proxy completeness to the causal information that remains in sharp bounds.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Proxy information may not point-identify the effect -> nonidentification need not mean no information -> observed proxy restrictions can narrow causal effects -> derive sharp transported-effect bounds under the full latent-shift laws

method_exemplars.technique: Encode finite structural assignments and observed laws as polynomial constraints, then use dual relaxation and spatial branch-and-bound with epsilon-sharpness certificates.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The destination is finite and discrete, but shared latent channels and cross-domain invariances create nonlinear factorization constraints suited to polynomial programming.

method_exemplars.technique: Adapt smooth approximations of nonsmooth proxy-bound functionals and bootstrap confidence intervals for their endpoints.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The sharp transport endpoints will likewise be nonsmooth value functions of estimated observed-law constraints.

method_exemplars.technique: Adapt sum-of-ratios reformulation and globally convergent branch-and-bound over latent mixture and proxy-channel variables.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Its optimization geometry directly resembles latent-channel factorization, while the destination adds multiple source domains and exact target-law matching.

open_problems.open_problem: If the proxy channel M=P(W|U) is rank-deficient, exactly when does the transported causal effect remain identified despite simultaneous nonuniqueness of the target latent mixture and the source factorization?

source_refs.claim: The paper groups latent states into proxy-induced equivalence classes and uses full-rank source mixtures over those classes to identify a target predictor, not a target-specific causal functional over all compatible factorizations.
source_refs.author: Zahra Rahiminasab, Reza Soumi, Arto Klami, Samuel Kaski

source_refs.claim: The nullspace-orthocomplement theorem handles functional uniqueness on one bridge-solution fiber, not the nested fiber of unknown proxy channel, source factorization, and target mixture.
source_refs.author: Jeffrey Zhang, Wei Li, Wang Miao, Eric Tchetgen Tchetgen

source_refs.claim: The paper shows proxy restrictions can still bound causal effects after completeness fails, but does not give a transport-specific point-identification quotient over unknown shared channels.
source_refs.author: AmirEmad Ghassami, Ilya Shpitser, Eric Tchetgen Tchetgen

source_refs.excerpt: Future proximal topics should build on that result
which observed bridge-null directions lift to a valid finite latent negative-control law

open_problems.why_unsolved: The finite target-span sufficiency proof uses injectivity of M to infer equality of latent mixtures from equality of proxy mixtures. With ker(M) nontrivial, Q(W) indexes an affine family of target latent laws and B_x=MR_x may have multiple positive factorizations. Rahiminasab et al. quotient latent states by proxy equivalence classes for prediction, while Zhang et al. treat one inverse equation; neither controls causal outcome variation within an equivalence class across every compatible factorization. Prior reviewers further warn that positivity and common-mechanism restrictions can make the realizable causal kernel smaller than the algebraic kernel. The first proof step that changes is therefore the injectivity argument, which must become a nested quotient over jointly feasible perturbations of q, R_x, M, and the response mechanism.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A necessary-and-sufficient theorem characterizing constancy of the transported intervention functional over all strictly positive factorizations compatible with the supplied source and target laws, with a finite quotient/nullspace certificate on success and paired full-law SCM countermodels on failure.

writing_exemplar.why: Its latent-equivalence-class framing is the closest destination-area language for imperfect proxies, while the new destination is explicitly causal rather than predictive.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Imperfect proxies merge latent states -> full latent recovery and ordinary completeness fail -> source diversity may identify an equivalence-class functional -> determine whether the transported intervention law is constant on the full causal factorization fiber

method_exemplars.technique: Represent inverse solutions as an affine space plus an operator kernel and test target-functional constancy by annihilation.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The resolution must generalize this move from one bridge fiber to the jointly compatible fiber generated by ker(M), source-factor ambiguity, positivity, and invariant mechanisms.

method_exemplars.technique: Retain proxy restrictions after completeness failure and optimize the causal target over the remaining compatible class.
method_exemplars.why_closest: When the nested quotient does not annihilate the causal functional, the same object becomes a partial-identification region.

method_exemplars.technique: Construct orthogonal root-n inference for a linear functional through a dual representer despite nonunique inverse-problem nuisances.
method_exemplars.why_closest: On the identified branch, inference should depend on stability of the quotient functional rather than unique recovery of M, q, or R_x.

literature_map:
1. Iglesias-Alonso, Schur, von Kügelgen, and Peters (NeurIPS 2025, arXiv:2510.25924) is the exact anchor: full source rank gives a proxy-balancing functional, pointwise inference, and the Expedia ranking application.
2. Its Appendix B.2 makes P(W|U) rank-deficient for generic nonidentification; it does not settle deficient source rank with an injective proxy or target-specific span membership.
3. Zhang, Li, Miao, and Tchetgen Tchetgen (Statistics & Probability Letters 2023, arXiv:2303.10134), Proposition 2.3, proves null-annihilator functional identification; Lemma 2.4 strengthens closure to actual adjoint range for root-n estimation.
4. Rahiminasab, Soumi, Klami, and Kaski (2026, arXiv:2603.15158), Theorem 3, identifies a target predictor by spanning proxy-induced latent-equivalence-class operators, but assumes full source rank at that quotient level.
5. Tsai et al. (AISTATS 2024, arXiv:2403.07442) and Alabdulmohsin et al. (AISTATS 2023, arXiv:2212.11254) provide the latent-shift/proxy domain-adaptation lineage, generally under completeness or full diversity.
6. Miao, Geng, and Tchetgen Tchetgen (Biometrika 2018, DOI 10.1093/biomet/asy038) is the foundational finite proxy-rank causal-ID result; Cui et al. (JASA 2024, arXiv:2011.08411) supplies proximal efficiency theory.
7. Bennett et al. (COLT 2023, arXiv:2208.08291) directly studies strongly identified functionals of weakly identified or nonunique inverse-problem nuisances and is the closest route to a weak-rank regularity frontier.
8. Santos (Journal of Econometrics 2011, DOI 10.1016/j.jeconom.2010.11.014) and Severini–Tripathi (Journal of Econometrics 2012, DOI 10.1016/j.jeconom.2012.05.018) supply NPIV precedents for identified functionals and efficiency without nuisance identification.
9. Dufour–Taamouti (Econometrica 2005), Mikusheva (Journal of Econometrics 2010), and Andrews–Guggenberger (Quantitative Economics 2019) supply projection, weak-ID-uniform, and covariance-singularity-robust inference tools.
10. Their unresolved tension here is nuisance geometry: IV projection is model-specific, while general singularity-robust subvector theory assumes strongly identified nuisance parameters; transport weights may be nonunique and unbounded.
11. Zhang–Su (UAI 2024, arXiv:2210.09885), Ghassami–Shpitser–Tchetgen Tchetgen (arXiv:2304.04374), and Duarte et al. (JASA 2024, arXiv:2109.13471) give proxy or general-SCM bounding machinery, but not this full multi-domain shared-channel factorization.
12. Mastouri et al. (ICML 2021, arXiv:2105.04544) and Ghassami et al. (AISTATS 2022, arXiv:2104.02929) provide continuous-proxy inverse-problem estimators useful for later operator extensions.
13. Ursu (Marketing Science 2018, DOI 10.1287/mksc.2017.1072) supplies the Expedia randomized-ranking benchmark and establishes the substantive endogeneity of ranking position.
14. Early-kill result: Zhang Proposition 2.3 subsumes solution independence but not the SCM converse; Rahiminasab Theorem 3 is a close full-rank prediction analogue but not the deficient-source-rank, target-specific interventional iff.
